student_thinking: Use $k\Delta x=mg$ to eliminate $k/m$
Substitute into $T=2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$

key_conditions.condition: the model assumptions stated in the stem hold
key_conditions.evidence: the stem states the model assumptions

misconceptions.description: Uses $2\pi\sqrt{2\Delta x/g}$, adding a factor of two.
Uses $2\pi\sqrt{g/\Delta x}$, inverting the ratio.
Omits the square root, $2\pi\Delta x/g$.

verification.independent_path: an RK4 integration with $k/m=g/\Delta x$ recomputes the period

ap_physics_c_mechanics-m109.stem: An object hangs at rest from a vertical ideal spring and stretches it by $20\text{ cm}$ at equilibrium. The object is then pulled down a small distance and released. What is the period of the oscillation? (The mass and the spring constant are not given.)

options.why: Uses $2\pi\sqrt{g/\Delta x}$, inverting the ratio.
$k/m=g/\Delta x$, so $T=2\pi\sqrt{\Delta x/g}=0.898\text{ s}$.
Omits the square root, $2\pi\Delta x/g$.
Uses $2\pi\sqrt{2\Delta x/g}$, adding a factor of two.

ap_physics_c_mechanics-m110.stem: A block oscillates on an ideal spring. The amplitude is multiplied by $2$. By what factor does the total mechanical energy change?

options.why: $E\propto A^2$ and $v_{max}\propto A$, so the factor is $4.00$.
Scales as the cube of the amplitude.
Does not change.
Scales as the root of the amplitude.

blueprint.subject: ap_physics_c_mechanics
blueprint.concept: Scaling of energy and maximum speed with amplitude
student_thinking: Write $E=\tfrac12kA^2$ and $v_{max}=A\sqrt{k/m}$
Apply the amplitude factor

key_conditions.condition: the model assumptions stated in the stem hold
key_conditions.evidence: the stem states the model assumptions

misconceptions.description: Scales as the cube of the amplitude.
Does not change.
Scales as the root of the amplitude.

verification.independent_path: the energy and the maximum speed are evaluated numerically for both amplitudes
